English: Earthen Pit
A simple storage pit dug into the ground, lined with straw and clay—an age-old solution for preserving grain and supplies in the earliest days of the nomad encampment.
Woven Basket
Large, tightly-woven baskets of reed and grass, carried on wagons or sleds, allow for mobile, above-ground storage and a modest increase in goods preservation.
Mudbrick Hut
Crude huts constructed of sun-baked mudbrick and thatch provide more durable storage, keeping out the elements and increasing the encampments capacity.
Raised Silo
Granaries built on timber stilts, with slatted floors, keep grain dry and safe from flood and vermin. This marks a shift to more sophisticated and semi-permanent food storage.
Guarded Storehouse
A fortified structure of timber and clay, watched by loyal guards, ensures the safety of supplies and wealth, deterring thieves and bolstering clan security.
Rodent-Proof Hut
Constructed with smooth, stone-lined walls and sealed doors, these granaries are nearly impervious to pests, significantly reducing spoilage and waste.
Expanded Store
A greatly enlarged and compartmentalized storehouse, able to handle surpluses and trade goods, supporting a growing and prosperous nomadic clan.
Market Pavilion
A bustling open-air tent market, where merchants and clansfolk gather to barter and trade, greatly boosting the encampments economic vibrancy.
Grain Exchange Hall
A permanent, timber-framed hall that acts as a central hub for the buying, selling, and storing of grain and goods, drawing merchants from afar and enriching the clan.
Indo-Aryan Granary
A monumental granary structure, inspired by the ancient storehouses of the Indus, able to sustain a vast nomadic population and project the clans wealth and unity across the steppe.
